summary: Zhang et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.08788v3; position paper subtitled 'Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate—We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity') is the corpus's decisive matched-compute reappraisal. DESIGN: 5 MAD frameworks (SoM=Du et al. 2023, Multi-Persona, Exchange-of-Thoughts, ChatEval, AgentVerse) x 9 benchmarks (general knowledge: MMLU, MMLU-Pro, CommonsenseQA, ARC-Challenge, AGIEval; math: GSM8K, MATH; programming: HumanEval, MBPP) x 4 models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-haiku, Llama3.1-8b, Llama3.1-70b), vs SA/CoT/SC baselines, debate rounds adjusted so every MAD method uses ~6 LLM calls; 3 repetitions with std (===== PDF PAGE 1, 6, 7 =====). HEADLINE: no MAD method exceeds a 20% win rate vs CoT across 36 scenarios; SoM/EoT/ChatEval/AgentVerse win ~15%, MP 0%; worse on programming, relatively better on math; the gap widens vs self-consistency at comparable LLM-call or token budgets (===== PDF PAGE 3, 7-8 =====). RECONCILIATION: MAD beats direct single-agent prompting in 34/45 GPT-4o-mini conditions—'perfectly aligns with previous findings'—but SoM and ChatEval were never compared to CoT in their original papers, so Du-style positives hold only against the weakest baseline (===== PDF PAGE 8 =====). HYPERPARAMETERS: agents 3->9, rounds 2->4 yield mostly stagnation or decline (sole exception EoT on GSM8K), ruling out misconfiguration as a universal explanation (===== PDF PAGE 8-9 =====). EFFICIENCY: SC converts extra tokens into accuracy; MAD is flat (SoM on MMLU) or trails SC at comparable tokens (EoT); per-question analysis shows aggressive methods (MP/ChatEval/AgentVerse) correct many errors but flip many correct answers, while conservative ones (SoM/EoT) avoid new errors but correct few—a correction/instability trade-off (===== PDF PAGE 9, 25 =====). HETEROGENEITY: Heter-MAD (each generation queries a random model from {GPT-4o-mini, Llama3.1-70b}, p=0.5) improves every tested framework (+6.4% SoM, +8.2% EoT vs single-model averages; up to +5.8% vs CoT-Average), with gains concentrated where models have complementary solvability and in simpler frameworks—'a universal antidote' (===== PDF PAGE 1, 4, 10-13 =====). POSITIONING: credits Du et al. 2023 as foundational but attributes MAD's overvaluation to fragmented, selective evaluation (Table 5 shows minimal benchmark overlap across prior MAD papers); aligns with Smit et al. 2024's null while dismissing its medical-only scope; flags that agents debate whole responses yet rebut final-answer differences rather than reasoning, and that current benchmarks need only single knowledge points (===== PDF PAGE 2, 5, 13, 14, 15 =====). Key identification gap for the root note: no heterogeneous self-consistency control, so the debate-specific value of heterogeneity over plain decorrelated sampling is not identified.
unresolved: Whether heterogeneous self-consistency (mixed-model sampling + majority vote, no communication) matches Heter-MAD at matched calls/tokens — the control needed to attribute heterogeneity gains to debate rather than to error decorrelation alone.

Why aggressive MAD variants flip initially correct answers: Zhang's corrected/erred analysis is behavioral and cannot distinguish social-influence conformity (Lorenz/Choi-style) from noise amplification or judge/aggregation failures.
Whether task topology (benchmarks requiring multiple, complementary knowledge points) reverses the MAD vs SC ordering — Zhang conjectures yes ('===== PDF PAGE 14 =====') but tests nothing.
